summary: Support addWord(word) and search(pattern) where '.' matches any single letter.
mainInsight: Store words in a trie. search walks the trie character by character; for '.' it tries every child (DFS/backtracking). Each non-wildcard step follows a single child.

approaches.name: List of words
approaches.summary: Compare each pattern with every word.

approaches.name: Trie + DFS for wildcards
approaches.timeComplexity: O(L) add, up to O(26^dots * L) search

commonMistakes: Treating '.' as zero or many characters

promptVariants: Which technique solves this problem, and what in the statement or constraints points to it?
Name the technique you would use here and the clue in the problem that tells you.
What approach fits this problem, and which part of the statement gives it away?
cards.answer: Trie with DFS for wildcards: follow one child per letter and try every child at a '.'. Clue: Words are added over time and searched by a pattern where '.' stands for any letter, and at most two dots appear, so a prefix tree can follow letters and branch only at the dots.
keyPoints: Words are added over time and searched by a pattern where '.' stands for any letter, and at most two dots appear, so a prefix tree can follow letters and branch only at the dots.
cards.explanation: A trie shares prefixes, so a search only explores the few branches the wildcards open.

promptVariants: How should the search handle the '.' wildcard in a trie?
options: Recursively try every child of the current node
Skip the character without moving down the trie
Stop the search and return True
cards.answer: Recursively try every child of the current node
cards.explanation: '.' consumes one character and may take any branch.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Skip the character without moving down t: The wildcard stands for exactly one letter.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Stop the search and return True: The remaining characters must still match.

promptVariants: Why is an end-of-word flag needed in each trie node?
Which pattern would give a false positive without it?
cards.answer: A path may spell a prefix of a stored word. For example after adding 'apple' the search 'app' reaches a node but is not a word, so only nodes marked as word ends count as matches.
cards.explanation: Return node.is_end at the last character.
addWord is O(L); search is O(L) without wildcards and up to O(26^k * L) with k dots.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: The trie stores the characters of all inserted words.
